You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Dow Inc. realized record, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window is the registrant's own realized
> record roughly three to five years after the ~2019 closing; the facts below are drawn
> from the registrant's annual report for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023 (the
> five-year mark). This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was
> structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status in the outcome window
- The registrant remained an SEC-reporting public company throughout the window and filed an annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K (fiscal year ended December 31, 2023)]
- The filing is a combined annual report for Dow Inc. and its subsidiaries and The Dow Chemical Company and its subsidiaries. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023]

## Realized financial trajectory (fiscal 2021-2023)
- Net sales were $44,622 million in 2023, $56,902 million in 2022, and $54,968 million in 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023, Consolidated Statements of Income]
- Net income available for Dow Inc. common stockholders was $589 million in 2023, $4,582 million in 2022, and $6,311 million in 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023, Consolidated Statements of Income]
- Diluted earnings per common share were $0.82 in 2023, $6.28 in 2022, and $8.38 in 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023, Consolidated Statements of Income]
- Income before income taxes was $656 million in 2023, $6,090 million in 2022, and $8,145 million in 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023, Consolidated Statements of Income]
- Restructuring and asset related charges - net were $528 million in 2023, $118 million in 2022, and $6 million in 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023, Consolidated Statements of Income]

## Operating realignment in the window
- In January 2023 the Board approved restructuring actions (the "2023 Restructuring Program") to achieve structural cost improvement initiatives in response to the continued economic impact from the global recessionary environment and to enhance the Company's agility. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023]
- Under the 2023 Restructuring Program the Company recorded pretax restructuring charges of $535 million, consisting of severance and related benefit costs of $344 million and asset write-downs and write-offs of $191 million; the severance related to a global workforce reduction of approximately 2,000 employees, with the majority of separations occurring by the end of the second quarter of 2023 and the remainder primarily through the end of 2024. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023]
- Equity in earnings (losses) of nonconsolidated affiliates moved to a loss of $119 million in 2023 from earnings of $268 million in 2022, described as primarily due to declines at Sadara and the Kuwait joint ventures. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023]

## Workforce and operations in the window
- At December 31, 2023, the Company permanently employed approximately 35,900 people on a full-time basis. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023]
- The Company states that Dow operates manufacturing sites in 31 countries and delivered sales of approximately $45 billion in 2023. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023]

## Reference to the separation agreements (context, not the outcome scalar)
- The FY2023 filing references agreements entered into with DuPont and Corteva as part of the separation and distribution (related to Corporate); these are noted only as context and are not the outcome scalar reported above. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Over the fixed ~2021-2023 window the registrant's net sales moved from $54,968 million (2021) to a peak of $56,902 million (2022) and then to $44,622 million (2023), while net income available for Dow Inc. common stockholders declined from $6,311 million (2021) to $4,582 million (2022) to $589 million (2023); the 2023 result included $528 million of net restructuring and asset related charges under a Board-approved 2023 Restructuring Program ($535 million pretax; ~2,000-employee workforce reduction), the registrant permanently employed approximately 35,900 people at December 31, 2023, and it continued to operate as an independent SEC-reporting company across the window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001751788-24-000010, Form 10-K FY2023]

[SLICE END]
